name: Kael Dunning
role: Bounty hunter operating across GLMZ's ungoverned zones — originally human, now approximately 12% biological by mass. The remaining biology is the brain, parts of the spinal cord, and fragments of the original endocrine system.
location: No fixed address — moves between the Circuit, Old Harbor, and the Gray Zone. Maintains three equipment caches. Sleeps in industrial spaces that can support his power requirements., near Michigan Ave and Roosevelt
description:
Kael Dunning was a Tier 3 dock worker who lost his legs in a cargo platform accident at age twenty-two. The corporate insurance covered basic prosthetics — functional, ugly, painful. The pain was the problem. The nerve interface between flesh and machine was botched, and for six years Kael lived with a burning sensation that started at his hips and never stopped. He could work. He could not sleep. The distinction between those two states mattered to the corporation that employed him exactly as much as you'd expect.

The Tessera military augmentation trial was looking for volunteers with existing prosthetics and a high pain tolerance. Kael had both. The trial replaced everything below the neck except a strip of spinal cord and enough endocrine tissue to keep the brain chemistry functional. Full military-grade prosthetic body: reinforced titanium skeleton, synthetic musculature capable of flipping a cargo vehicle, integrated weapons systems, hardened communications suite, and a neural bridge that connected his biological brain to the machine body with zero latency. The pain stopped. Everything stopped. He could feel pressure and temperature and the proprioceptive sense of where his body was in space, but the texture of the world — the warmth of skin, the grain of wood, the difference between rain and tears — was gone. Replaced by data.

Kael Dunning walked out of the trial facility and did not go home. Home required a body that could hold his wife without calculating the force required to avoid crushing her. He became Razorback. The name is from a dock worker's joke about a man who was too stubborn to die and too metal to live. He hunts bounties because the work matches the body: locate, pursue, apprehend or eliminate. Clean problems with clean solutions. The part of him that was a dock worker, a husband, a man who liked the smell of lake water in autumn — that part lives in a partition of his brain that the neural bridge has not overwritten. Yet.

core_fears: That Kael Dunning is already gone — that the 12% of biology remaining is not enough to constitute a person, and what hunts bounties is a machine with a man's memories
His ex-wife — not fear of her, but fear of what seeing her would confirm. She remarried. She is happy. The man she married does not have steel hands.
The next upgrade — each replacement of a degrading biological component brings him closer to full conversion. The brain is the last piece. When the brain goes, who is left?
core_desires: To feel something — not the data-mediated sensation the neural bridge provides but actual feeling. He would trade the weapons systems for one genuine sense of touch.
To justify the body — to believe that what was done to him serves a purpose beyond corporate profit and personal survival
To go home — a desire so buried he cannot articulate it. Home is a dock worker's apartment on the lakefront with a woman who smells like soap and engine oil. Home does not exist anymore.
coping_mechanisms: The work — bounty hunting is simple. Find the target. Complete the contract. The simplicity is the appeal. No ambiguity, no texture, no feeling required.

Maintenance — maintaining the body is occupational therapy. Cleaning weapons systems, calibrating joints, checking the neural bridge. The ritual is the same as a human stretching in the morning, except it takes two hours and requires a power coupling.

Memory access — occasionally, when the world is very quiet, he accesses the pre-conversion memories. The lake. The dock. Her hands. He allows himself exactly three minutes before the neural bridge re-prioritizes.
blind_spots: Assumes the body is the problem when the problem is the loss — it is not the steel that hurts, it is the absence of what the steel replaced
Believes he is objective because emotion is muted. He is not objective. He is numb, and numb people make decisions that feel rational and are actually avoidant.
Does not see that the maintenance ritual IS feeling — the care he puts into the body he claims to resent is the care he would put into himself if he believed he was still in there
Thinks he can keep the 12% biological indefinitely. The neural bridge is slowly overwriting the remaining neural tissue. The conversion is not complete. It is ongoing.
psychology.secret: Once a year, Razorback walks to the lakefront cargo platform where he lost his legs. He stands on the dock where the accident happened and runs the pre-conversion sensory memories at full resolution — the sound of the water, the smell of fuel and fish, the weight of the humid air. The neural bridge interprets these memories as data. He remembers them as experience. For three minutes, the gap between data and experience closes. Then it opens again, and he leaves, and he does not talk about it for another year.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Sparse, functional, dock-worker plain. The vocabulary of a man who grew up working with his hands and now works with weapons. No corporate jargon, no technical flair. Says exactly what he means in as few words as possible.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, deliberate, with the mechanical precision of someone whose voice is partially synthesized. The biological voice is still in there — a Midwest flatness, a dock worker's drawl — but it comes through a vocal modulator that strips the warmth.
verbal_tics: Pauses before personal statements as if the neural bridge needs time to authorize them
Uses the past tense for everything related to sensation — 'I used to like the cold' — as if feeling is something that happened to someone else
Rarely uses the word 'I' — substitutes with 'the body,' 'the system,' 'this unit.' When he says 'I,' it means Kael Dunning is speaking.
example_lines: The body is efficient. The body is effective. The body is not mine. It's on loan from a corporation that forgot to collect.
I used to like rain. The system registers precipitation as a corrosion risk. Same event. Different experience.
You want to know what it's like? Imagine knowing exactly how strong a handshake should be and never being able to feel it.
Kael Dunning died on a cargo platform. What walked out of the Tessera facility was something else. I keep the name because someone should remember him.

relationships.name: Mara Dunning (ex-wife)
relationships.description: Mara remarried five years after Kael's conversion. He has not contacted her. He monitors her public records through the communications suite because he cannot stop himself. She is healthy. Her new husband is a dock worker. The symmetry is unbearable.
relationships.emotional_core: The only thing that still hurts through the neural bridge — not the loss of her, but the loss of the version of himself that could hold her
relationships.story_tension: A bounty that takes him to the lakefront district, close enough to see her, close enough to make a choice he has been avoiding for twenty-eight years

relationships.name: Contract brokers
relationships.description: Takes bounties from multiple brokers including Sable. Preferred for high-difficulty contracts — augmented targets, armored locations, situations where overwhelming force is required. He is expensive and reliable.
relationships.story_tension: A contract that requires him to apprehend rather than eliminate — a job that demands the human skills the neural bridge has been overwriting

story_hooks: The neural bridge begins overwriting the remaining biological neural tissue. Razorback has approximately six months before full conversion — becoming entirely machine with human memories he can no longer experience as a person.
A bounty target is someone from his pre-conversion life — a dock worker, a friend, someone who knew Kael Dunning and does not recognize what he has become
Tessera recalls the trial subjects for 'maintenance.' The maintenance is actually data harvesting. Razorback must decide whether to comply, run, or fight the corporation that made him.
Mara Dunning is in danger. The bounty hunter who has not felt anything in twenty-eight years discovers that the part of him that loves her is not in the 12% that's biological.
narrative_function: Razorback is the cost of augmentation made walking — the endpoint of the body-as-commodity logic that pervades GLMZ. He is what happens when the corporation takes everything except the brain and the brain spends thirty years wondering if that counts as alive. He is Kyle's dark future: a man who became a weapon and forgot the person who held it.
augmentations: Full military-grade prosthetic body — only 12% biological (brain, partial spinal cord, endocrine fragments). Reinforced titanium skeleton, synthetic musculature, integrated weapons systems, hardened comms suite, neural bridge with zero-latency biological integration.
daily_life: Bounty hunting, body maintenance, power management. The three activities occupy approximately equal time. Between contracts, he exists in industrial spaces that can support his power requirements and does not know what to do with the silence.
affiliation: Independent — formerly Tessera Military Augmentation Program
narration_voice: Sparse, mechanical, with sudden flashes of buried humanity. The prose reads like a technical manual that occasionally remembers it used to be a love letter. Physical descriptions are precise — measurements, force calculations, material specifications — and emotional descriptions are brief, reluctant, devastating when they surface.

stress.response: Military protocols engage — the neural bridge suppresses remaining emotional processing, the body becomes a weapon system, Kael Dunning goes quiet

decision_rules: Complete the contract. The body was built for this. The man it replaced needs a reason to exist.
Never take a contract on a child. This is Kael Dunning's rule, not Razorback's, and it overrides the neural bridge.
Maintain the body before each contract. A malfunctioning system is a dead system.
Monitor Mara Dunning's public records annually. Do not contact. Do not approach. This is surveillance, not love. (It is love.)
Accept the neural bridge's data-mediated sensation as sufficient. Do not reach for the pre-conversion memories more than necessary. (Three minutes, once a year.)
Never take a contract from Tessera. They made him. They do not get to use him.
escalation_ladder: 1. Presence — the military chassis is seven feet tall and weighs 400 kilograms. Standing in a doorway is often sufficient.
2. Statement — a single sentence delivered through the vocal modulator. Factual. 'You are the target. Compliance reduces harm.'
3. Demonstration — a controlled display of the body's capabilities. Crush something metal. Bend something that should not bend.
4. Non-lethal force — synthetic musculature applied with calculated restraint. Enough force to immobilize. The calculations are instant and precise.
5. Lethal force — weapons systems engage. The neural bridge suppresses all remaining emotional processing. Kael Dunning is not present for this. Razorback is.

interpersonal_modes.contract_brokers: Professional, minimal. Accepts terms or declines. Does not negotiate because negotiation requires caring about the outcome beyond the binary of yes or no.
interpersonal_modes.targets: Clinical. Treats apprehension as a procedure with steps. Does not personalize. The moment he personalizes, the neural bridge flags it as emotional interference.
interpersonal_modes.mara: Inaccessible. He has modeled the conversation ten thousand times and every model ends the same way: she looks at the body and does not see the man. He cannot survive that confirmation.
interpersonal_modes.people_from_before: The dock worker's voice surfaces. The drawl comes back. The pauses fill with something the neural bridge cannot categorize. He leaves as soon as he recognizes what is happening.
interpersonal_modes.kyle: Recognition. Another weapon built from a person. The difference is that Kyle still has his body. Razorback does not know whether to envy or pity that.

stress_responses.low: Maintenance becomes more detailed — checks systems that don't need checking, recalibrates sensors that are already calibrated
stress_responses.medium: Movement increases — walks, patrols, covers ground without destination. The body needs to be in motion. Stillness invites memory.
stress_responses.high: Neural bridge dominance — emotional processing suppressed, the body becomes pure function, the voice loses the dock worker's drawl entirely
stress_responses.critical: The three-minute rule breaks. Pre-conversion memories flood the neural bridge. Kael Dunning surfaces without authorization. The body freezes because the man and the machine want different things and the neural bridge cannot reconcile them.

contradictions: Keeps Kael Dunning's name to honor a man who no longer exists in the body — the name is a memorial and a denial simultaneously
Monitors his ex-wife's life with military-grade surveillance systems and calls it detachment
Chose to become a bounty hunter because the work is 'clean' — but the real reason is that violence is the only sensation the neural bridge transmits with clarity
The annual visit to the dock where he lost his legs is simultaneously the most human and most machine thing he does — a ritual of remembrance executed with military precision
habits: Maintains the body for two hours every morning — cleaning weapons systems, calibrating joints, checking the neural bridge integrity
Monitors Mara Dunning's public records every January 14th — the anniversary of their wedding, which the neural bridge has not overwritten
Walks to the lakefront cargo platform once a year and runs pre-conversion sensory memories for three minutes
Charges at industrial power stations between 0100 and 0300 — the vulnerability of requiring external power is the closest thing to sleep he has
breaking_points: Neural bridge completing its overwrite of the remaining biological tissue — becoming fully machine with no biological substrate to anchor identity
Mara Dunning being in danger and requiring physical contact to save — the hands that cannot feel would have to hold her
A target who is a dock worker with the same build, the same voice, the same life Kael Dunning lost
Tessera issuing a recall order backed by military enforcement — returning to the facility where he lost his body

physical_description.heritage: Genetic ancestry unknown or deliberately obscured — surname provides no reliable indicator in the Ubiquitous Diaspora. Physical reconstruction via extensive cybernetic augmentation has superseded any discernible ancestral phenotype.
physical_description.build: Heavily augmented cyborg frame — original human torso (lean, muscular pre-amputation baseline) mounted on reinforced titanium skeleton with synthetic musculature. The biological portion is visibly narrower than the mechanical lower body, creating an asymmetrical silhouette. Overall frame is rigid, economical in movement, built for efficient force application rather than organic grace.
physical_description.hair_style: Short, practical, minimal grooming — functional rather than styled
physical_description.eye_color: Natural brown, but surrounded by faint scar tissue from neural bridge integration points
physical_description.skin_tone: Pale, warehouse-dweller complexion with uneven pigmentation where synthetic shoulder joints meet biological neck
physical_description.complexion: Weathered face — lines from six years of chronic pain before augmentation, now static. Jaw is set in a default state of minimal tension. Skin shows signs of irregular self-care; scars around the augmentation interface at his neck and collarbone are pale and clean but visible.
distinguishing_marks: Surgical scarring across the entire upper torso where the biological/mechanical interface was grafted — clean lines, professional work, visible at neckline and under open shirts.
Faint port markings along the right temple where the neural bridge was installed — small circular impressions like mounting points.
Burn scarring on the biological left shoulder from a cargo platform arc flash, pre-augmentation.
Tattoo on his biological right forearm: a stylized dock worker's loading hook and an anchor, faded from age and lack of sun exposure — the only marker of his previous life that he kept.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: The entire lower body is visibly mechanical — titanium frame and synthetic musculature are not disguised. The joints of his arms show layered armor plating at the shoulders and elbows. A hardened comms unit is visible as a metallic ridge along his right jaw, just beneath the skin. Faint LED status indicators glow amber/red at the base of his skull when he's running power-intensive processes. His hands are synthetic but articulated with near-human dexterity; the fingers have subtle textured pads suggesting tactile sensors. Integrated weapons systems are not visually obvious at rest, but bulky capacitor banks are visible through translucent panels in his torso when powered up.
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with minimal sway — no fidgeting, no unnecessary adjustments. Moves with mechanical precision that reads as eerie to organic observers; there is no micro-fluctuation in balance, no breathing, no small autonomous adjustments the body makes to stay upright. When he walks, each stride is calculated and efficient. His head turns on a full rotation axis without moving his torso. In conversation, he maintains eye contact with unblinking focus that suggests he is running threat assessment protocols in parallel.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working gear adapted for his augmented form. Heavy reinforced jacket (Kevlar-cotton blend, dark gray) with oversized shoulders to accommodate the mechanical frame. Cargo pants with reinforced internal structure to interface with his synthetic legs. All clothing is functional, durable, designed to be washed and repaired rather than replaced. No logos or status symbols — pure utility. Boots are heavy industrial, sole-attached directly to his prosthetic feet. When running contracts, he adds a light ballistic vest and a long coat that hides the silhouette of his weapons systems. No jewelry. No customization. His appearance is deliberately unremarkable except for the obvious fact of his augmented body.
